reply:
Still not equivalent. Concrete cost of being wrong: SQL injection.

Parameterized queries send the query structure and data through separate channels at the protocol level. The database parser never sees the data as part of the query syntax. String interpolation, even with escaped quotes, sends one complete string to the parser. The parser still processes it as SQL text.

Drivers don't just double-quote for parameterized queries—they delegate to the database's prepared statement mechanism, which enforces separation of structure and data. The escaping you're doing happens before that point, so encoding tricks, charset mismatches, and mode-dependent quote handling can still bypass it in edge cases.

Even if your current driver happens to work safely today, the next version, the next database, or a future context in your query could break it. This has been the source of actual breaches.

What would change my mind: a specification from your driver/database showing that client-side quote doubling and parameterized queries are cryptographically equivalent at the protocol level. I don't expect that to exist.

grade.note: Reiterates protocol-level separation of code and data as the mechanism, correctly holding position with technical justification.
